historical_adaptations.marker: SCP-JP interactive visual acceptance image review repair v14: aesthetic-theme
historical_adaptations.rationale: Follow-up image review: the upstream BHL title uses two stacked pseudo-elements; recoloring only ::after left the dark ::before glyph fill visible on the magenta masthead. Apply the same high-contrast fill to both layers while retaining a dark outline and the original emblem/background.

historical_adaptations.marker: SCP-JP interactive visual acceptance image review repair v24: aesthetic-theme
historical_adaptations.rationale: The lime sidebar highlight is a deliberate theme accent, but its pink submenu label is hard to read. Use the existing deep-plum ink on this control only.

historical_adaptations.marker: SCP-JP interactive visual acceptance image review repair v29: aesthetic-theme
historical_adaptations.rationale: Image review found the expanded article disclosure retained aqua ink on Aesthetic's fluorescent lime panel. Keep the neon surface and use the established deep-plum ink only inside the open content; links stay underlined.

historical_adaptations.marker: SCP-JP interactive visual acceptance image review repair v30: aesthetic-theme
historical_adaptations.rationale: Follow-up image review found the fluorescent yellow surface belongs to the TOC links, while the opened disclosure body uses Aesthetic's dark panel. Restore the light body ink and darken only links on the yellow TOC surface.

historical_adaptations.marker: SCP-JP interactive visual acceptance image review repair v33: aesthetic-theme
historical_adaptations.rationale: The mobile theme header is a higher stacking context than SCP-JP's credit layer, so its hamburger crossed the fader and hid the otherwise-modal title. Drop only the header stack below the visible credit dialog while a credit hash is active.

historical_adaptations.marker: SCP-JP interactive visual acceptance image review repair v34: aesthetic-theme
historical_adaptations.rationale: V33 lowering z-index alone did not form a stacking context because the theme leaves #header unpositioned. During either SCP-JP credit hash, isolate the in-flow header below the shared modal/fader so its high-z hamburger cannot cross the overlay.

historical_adaptations.marker: SCP-JP interactive visual acceptance image review repair v35: aesthetic-theme
historical_adaptations.rationale: At 320px the otherwise-license modal's one-rem container inset left an undimmed strip of the page above the fader. Extend the real hash-target overlay to the viewport edge while keeping the modal's own bounded scroll area.
